issue: Distractor (d) 'Settlement of a tax dispute for a year-end tax year at an amount different from the accrual' is explained as a Type I (recognized) event, but under U.S. GAAP a post-balance-sheet development on an uncertain income tax position (including a settlement with the taxing authority) is treated as a nonrecognized subsequent event. So (d) is also a defensible answer to 'Which subsequent event is nonrecognized?', and the explanation teaches the wrong rule. The wording 'for a year-end tax year' is also garbled.
evidence: Blind answer c (agrees with key), but (d) can't be eliminated: ASC 740-10-25-15 bases subsequent recognition, derecognition and measurement of a tax position on the information available at the reporting date, and changes in judgment go in the period they occur. PwC Viewpoint 'IFRS and US GAAP: similarities and differences' §8.8 (uncertain tax positions) contrasts the two frameworks: under U.S. GAAP, developments affecting uncertain tax positions after the balance sheet date but before issuance, including information not available at the balance sheet date, are a non-adjusting (nonrecognized) subsequent event. Under IFRS (IAS 10) they can be adjusting. Item (d)'s explanation ('it settles a tax position that existed at year-end, so it is recognized') applies the IFRS/ASC 855 general logic, which ASC 740 overrides for income-tax positions. If 'tax dispute' instead means a non-income tax (e.g., a property-tax assessment, ASC 450), (d) would be Type I, so the stem is ambiguous either way.
source: ASC 740-10-25-15; ASC 855-10-25-1; PwC Viewpoint, IFRS and US GAAP: similarities and differences §8.8, https://viewpoint.pwc.com/dt/us/en/pwc/accounting_guides/ifrs_and_us_gaap_sim/ifrs_and_us_gaap_sim_US/chapter_8_liabilitie_US/88_uncertain_tax_pos_US.html
fix: Replace (d) with an unambiguous recognized event that is not an income-tax position, e.g., 'Receipt in February of the final invoice for legal services performed in December, $15,000 more than accrued' (explanation: evidence about a year-end liability, so adjust). Alternatively, if a tax item is wanted, make it a property-tax assessment for the current year and say so. Never use an income-tax uncertain-position settlement as a Type I example.

issue: Pure rule recall is labeled skill 'analysis', difficulty 3 (two levels too high). se-26 asks 'Through what date does an SEC filer evaluate subsequent events?' with no fact pattern. se-24 asks whether EPS is restated for a post-year-end 2-for-1 split.
evidence: se-26 is the same question as se-03 ('An SEC registrant evaluates subsequent events through which date?'), which is labeled remembering, difficulty 1; the cues.md near-duplicate scan pairs se-26 with se-03 (0.50) and se-11 (0.80). se-24 restates fc4 / key takeaway 4 verbatim and needs no fact analysis. Under the Blueprint, recall of a rule is Remembering & Understanding, and Analysis means examining relationships among facts to draw inferences. Both items count toward FAR's 35-45% Analysis target when they should count toward the 5-15% R&U target.
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill definitions; FAR skill allocation in content/sections/far.yaml
fix: Set skill 'remembering' and difficulty 1 on far-se-24 and far-se-26 (or delete se-26 as a duplicate of se-03).

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are one level off on single-rule classification items. se-17, se-18, se-20, se-21, se-22, se-23, se-25, se-27 and se-28 are labeled analysis, difficulty 3, but each applies one rule to one stated fact (application, difficulty 1-2). se-11 and se-15 are pure rule recall labeled application (they should be remembering). The labels are also inverted against their near-twins.
evidence: Twin comparisons: se-21 (stem says outright 'financial decline that existed at year-end') is analysis/3, while se-01 (the student must infer that the condition existed from 'worsening for a year') is application/2, and x3-23 (same fact as se-21) is application/2. se-22 (February fire) is analysis/3, but se-16 (January fire, same facts) is application/2. se-25 ($5M bonds) is analysis/3, but se-12 ($10M bonds) is application/1. se-28 (post-YE market decline) is analysis/3, but se-14 (same facts) is application/2. se-23 (lawsuit settled above accrual) is analysis/3, but se-13 (same) is application/2. Labeled practice+exam mix: 2 R / 15 App / 13 An (6.7/50/43%). Relabeled honestly, roughly 6 R (se-03, se-08, se-11, se-15, se-24, se-26) / 22 App / 2 An (se-02, se-09): 20/73/7%. The module's apparent fit to the FAR Analysis target (35-45%) is an artifact of the labels.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprints skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel se-17, se-18, se-20, se-21, se-22, se-23, se-25, se-27 and se-28 as application with difficulty 1-2, matching their twins. Relabel se-11 and se-15 as remembering. To raise genuine analysis content, add multi-event items (see the coverage finding) rather than inflating labels.

issue: Heavy redundancy: the same handful of facts is tested the same way 3-5 times, and several practice items are near-verbatim duplicates. One exam-pool item duplicates a practice item, which inflates mock scores.
evidence: Clusters (item counts include options in other items): (1) Pre-YE customer deterioration leading to post-YE bankruptcy, so adjust the allowance: se-01, se-10, se-21, x3-23, plus x3-15(c) and the lesson big-idea example. x3-23 ('a major customer files for bankruptcy because of financial difficulties that existed at year-end') is se-21 reworded, so a learner who has practiced se-21 sees the answer in the mock. (2) Post-YE bond issuance, so disclose: se-12 ($10M) and se-25 ($5M) differ only in amount, plus se-06(c) and x3-15(a). (3) Pre-YE lawsuit settled after YE, so adjust: chk1, se-04, se-13, se-23 (se-13 and se-23 are both 'settles above accrual'), plus x3-15(b). (4) Post-YE warehouse fire, so disclose: pre1 and se-16 are the identical 'January 20 warehouse fire' scenario, and se-22 repeats it in February (cues.md Jaccard 0.64). (5) SEC-filer date: se-03 and se-26. Non-SEC date: chk2 and se-11 (cues.md se-11~se-26 0.80). (6) Post-YE market decline: chk1(b), se-14, se-28. (7) Stock split: se-05, se-24. Cross-module: far-cont-27 (contingencies) repeats se-09's 'lawsuit filed after YE for a pre-YE event'. Meanwhile, gaps go untested (see the coverage finding).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (same fact tested the same way more than about 3 times)
fix: Retire or rewrite the duplicates: se-16 (or change pre1), se-21, se-22, se-23, se-24, se-25, se-26 and se-28. Rewrite x3-23 so it does not mirror se-21 (e.g., an exam-style item with four mixed events). Reuse the slots for the untested sub-topics listed in the coverage finding.

issue: Trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models. 'partial-computation' is used on non-computational distractors. Distractors that push recognition into the next period are labeled 'wrong-rule' instead of 'wrong-period'. Identical misconceptions carry different labels across twin items.
evidence: se-05(a) 'No effect; disclose the split only', se-24(c) 'Disclosed only' and se-13(a) 'A liability of $200,000, with disclosure' all model treating a recognized item as nonrecognized (wrong-classification), yet each is labeled partial-computation. The same misconception in se-23(a) is labeled wrong-rule. se-08(b) 'Only the date on which the event occurred' is an incomplete disclosure, not a computation. se-21(d) 'Record it next year only', se-24(b) 'Adjusted next year' and se-27(b) 'Record the loss in January' are labeled wrong-rule, while the same error in se-01(c), se-04(c) and se-13(c) is labeled wrong-period.
fix: se-05(a), se-13(a), se-24(c): wrong-classification. se-08(b): wrong-rule (or other). se-21(d), se-24(b), se-27(b): wrong-period.

issue: Explanations are thin or circular and don't teach the rule or the computation. Several distractor rationales only say 'Not the treatment' or 'Not the effect'. The item-level explanations of the two settlement items don't show the adjustment.
evidence: se-22(d) and se-25(d): 'Not the treatment.' se-23(d): 'Not the effect.' se-20(b): 'That isn't what the rule says.' se-20(d): 'They're measured.' se-21(c): 'It affects the statements.' se-26(d): 'Not the rule for SEC filers.' (it doesn't say the audit report date is an auditing concept, AU-C 560/700). se-19(c): 'Not until declared.' The dividend was declared (Jan 15). The point is that declaration happened after the balance sheet date, so retained earnings is reduced in the next year. se-13 and se-23 item explanations state only the principle: neither shows the year-end adjustment (se-13: 260,000 - 200,000 = +60,000 loss and liability; se-23: 120,000 - 100,000 = +20,000), and neither cites ASC 855-10-55-1(a). se-20's item explanation doesn't cite ASC 740-10-35-4 / 740-10-45-15 (effect recognized in the enactment period).
fix: Rewrite each listed rationale to name the specific error. For example, se-23(d): 'A settlement above the accrual is an additional loss, never a gain'. se-25(d): 'Issuing debt is not an OCI item; the bonds are recorded when issued in February and disclosed in the December statements'. se-19(c): 'Retained earnings is reduced on the declaration date, January 15, so not at December 31'. Add the +60,000 / +20,000 computations and the ASC 855-10-55-1(a) citation to se-13 and se-23.

issue: calc is set to true on items that require no computation. The keyed amount is a figure given in the stem.
evidence: se-09: the keyed 'Accrue $200,000' is counsel's stated estimate, with no arithmetic. se-13: the key is the stated $260,000 settlement. se-23: the key is the stated $120,000 settlement. By contrast, se-04 (500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000) and se-10 (90,000 x 80% = 72,000) do require a computation and are correctly flagged.
source: src/content/schema.ts (calc: set only for items that need a computation); review brief §2 check 5
fix: Set calc false on far-se-09, far-se-13 and far-se-23. Alternatively, reword se-13/se-23 to ask for the adjustment amount (e.g., 'By how much should the December 31 liability be increased?', key 60,000 / 20,000), which keeps calc true legitimately.

issue: Answer cues from absolutes and hedging. The key is the only hedged or qualified option, and the distractors carry absolutes ('all', 'every', 'never', 'only', 'no ... unless').
evidence: se-15: (a) 'recognizes all events', (b) 'ignores all later events, even disclosure', (c) 'restates for every later event' against the key (d) 'doesn't recognize them unless GAAP or regulation requires'. The key is also by far the longest (cues.md: key much longest, absolutes only in distractors a,b,c), so a test-wise candidate picks (d) without knowing ASC 855-10-25-4. se-08: the key is the longest option, and (b) 'Only the date' and (d) 'No disclosure unless a user requests it' are absolutes. se-07(d): 'No action, because thefts are never material' is a give-away absolute.
fix: se-15: give the distractors qualified wording of similar length, e.g., (a) 'It recognizes events through the reissuance date that relate to year-end conditions', (b) 'It discloses later events but evaluates only through the original issuance date' (note: under 855-10-50-4/50-5 non-SEC entities disclose both dates), (c) 'It restates for any later event that is material'. se-08: replace (b)/(d) with plausible non-absolute disclosures, e.g., 'A pro forma balance sheet only, with no narrative' and 'The date through which events were evaluated only'. se-07(d): replace with 'Disclose the theft and record the loss when the insurance claim is settled'.

issue: Implausible distractors that no prepared candidate would choose, so these items are effectively three-option (or fewer) questions.
evidence: se-23(d) 'A $120,000 gain': settling a loss contingency above its accrual can't produce a gain. se-05(d) 'The split is recorded as a year-end liability'. se-18(d) 'Report it in OCI as a loss' (embezzlement). se-25(d) 'Recorded in OCI' (bond issuance). se-28(c) 'Recorded in OCI at year-end' (market decline after year-end, with no indication the securities are AFS debt). None of these models a misconception the topic actually produces.
fix: Replace with misconception-based options. se-23(d): 'A $120,000 liability, with the $20,000 increase charged to Year 2 earnings'. se-05(d): 'Share data restated, but prior-year EPS left unchanged'. se-18(d): 'Disclose only, because it was discovered after year-end'. se-25(d): 'Recognize the bond proceeds and liability at December 31 because the bonds were authorized in December'. se-28(c): 'Remeasure the investments to the February fair value because they are held for trading'. Don't use a debt-refinancing option: under ASC 470-10-45-14 a post-YE long-term refinancing can change year-end classification, so it would be a correct answer.

issue: The lesson leaves out parts of ASC 855 that its own items test or that its objective promises. (1) Reissued financial statements (855-10-25-4, 50-4/50-5) are never mentioned, yet se-15 (difficulty 3) tests them. (2) Objective 2 promises 'required disclosures', but the lesson only says 'disclose if material' and never states what the disclosure contains (855-10-50-2: nature of the event plus an estimate of its financial effect, or a statement that an estimate can't be made), which se-08 tests. (3) 'Issued' and 'available to be issued' are used but never defined (855-10-20). (4) The SEC-filer rule omits conduit bond obligors with publicly traded conduit debt (855-10-25-1A(b)).
evidence: Lesson body (731 words with frontmatter) has two tables, a timeline, a flowchart and one faded example. A search of lesson.md for 'reissu', 'nature', 'estimate', 'conduit' and 'approv' finds no match for any of these points. Without the 855-10-20 definitions (available to be issued = complete in a GAAP-compliant form with all approvals obtained, e.g., management, board, significant shareholders), a learner can't tell why a private company's window may end before the statements are actually issued.
fix: Add a short 'Disclosures and special cases' section. Cover: nonrecognized-event disclosure (nature plus estimate of effect, or a statement that no estimate can be made; pro forma data when very significant); definitions of issued and available to be issued; SEC filers and conduit bond obligors use the issued date; reissued statements don't recognize events after original issuance unless GAAP or regulation requires, and non-SEC entities disclose both evaluation dates. Add a matching key takeaway and flashcard.

issue: The practice pool (28 MCQs, 2 exam MCQs, no TBS) is almost all one-fact classification. Exam-level forms and several sub-topics are untested: no multi-event item asking for an adjusted amount (accrued liability, net income or total assets after several post-YE events); no Type II lawsuit arising from a post-YE event, although the lesson table and fc5 list it; no reissued-statement date disclosure; no item on the issued vs. available-to-be-issued definitions; no pro forma disclosure item.
evidence: All 30 practice/exam items are 'which treatment' or 'which date' questions. Only se-04 and se-10 involve arithmetic, and both are single-event. Grep of items.json finds no stem with a lawsuit whose underlying event occurred after year-end. The u12 contingencies TBS (far-tbs-u12-contingencies) touches subsequent events for one fact. On the 2026 exam, subsequent events usually appear as multi-event fact patterns (often inside a TBS or a 'what amount should be reported' MCQ), which the Blueprint task 'Identify and account for subsequent events' requires at application/analysis level.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint, Area III Group G (Subsequent events); ASC 855-10-55-1, 55-2
fix: Replace the duplicate items (see the redundancy finding) with: 2-3 multi-event computation MCQs (e.g., a 12/31 accrual of 300,000; a settlement at 420,000; a Feb flood loss of 250,000; a Jan customer bankruptcy from pre-YE deterioration on a 90,000 receivable with 20% recovery; ask for the total Year 1 pretax loss to recognize); one Type II post-YE-lawsuit item; one reissuance-dates item (non-SEC discloses both dates); and one item contrasting issued vs. available-to-be-issued dates. Consider a small subsequent-events TBS (classification dropdown plus a numeric adjustment).

issue: GASB Statement No. 105 (Subsequent Events), testable from Q3 2026, isn't mentioned anywhere in the content. This lesson presents ASC 855 without noting that governments follow separate GASB guidance.
evidence: review/reference/far-standards.md (GASB 105 row): issued Dec 2025, effective FY beginning after 6/15/2026, eligible for testing from 7/1/2026. It distinguishes recognized and nonrecognized events and specifies the note disclosures. grep -rni 'GASB 105' content/ returns no hits. FAR tests state and local government only at a foundational level, so this is a suggestion, not a gap in this module.
fix: Add a one-line note to this lesson: 'State and local governments follow GASB 105 (FY beginning after June 15, 2026), which uses the same recognized/nonrecognized split.' Leave fuller treatment to the far-government module.

issue: The stem is self-contradictory: 'a material portion of year-end inventory was stolen in November and never recorded'. Goods stolen in November weren't on hand at year-end. The intended meaning is that the recorded December 31 inventory balance included goods stolen in November.
evidence: The key (b) is correct under either reading (the loss occurred before the balance sheet date and was discovered before issuance), but 'never recorded' is ambiguous between 'the theft was never recorded' and 'the inventory was never recorded'.
fix: Reword: 'In February, before issuance, management discovers that inventory carried at $X in the December 31 records had been stolen in November; the loss was never recorded.'
